Sam / Priya — great to speak today. Quick recap and proposed next steps from our end so we keep momentum: 

Summary from call:
- You need a production-grade inference solution for FintechCo customer-facing workflows (credit decisioning + live chat).
- Main evaluation axes: latency at p50/p95, per-1M token TCO, and reliability (fallbacks/region).
- You are already evaluating HyperscaleCloud managed endpoints and an internal self-hosted prototype.

What Redwood can do next (proposed):
1) Run a short comparative POC (2 days) that measures throughput/latency and unit cost for a 1M-token workload across three configs: Redwood hosted (redwood-4x-32q), HyperscaleCloud standard, and your self-hosted baseline.
2) Measure batching (avg batch sizes 1, 4, 16) and prefix cache hit impact (we'll simulate 30/60/90% cache-hit scenarios).
3) Deliver a short TCO workbook with assumptions and token-level unit economics.

Attachments: comparison_table.xlsx (test matrix + suggested payloads).

Ask: Can you confirm a 2-day window next week for the live runs and a single test account with 5k sample prompts? If Procurement needs to be involved for the POC terms, loop them in — cc'd Priya.

If that works, I’ll assign an engineer to schedule the runs and we’ll add Marissa on the call for pricing cadence.

Ben

Sam — quick ballpark as requested, with assumptions called out below. Full workbook attached (unit_economics_assumptions.pdf).

High-level per-1M token (approx, USD):
- Redwood hosted (redwood-4x-32q, batching 4, cache hit 50%): $230 per 1M tokens
- HyperscaleCloud managed endpoint (avg config, batching 2, no prefix cache): $380 per 1M tokens
- Self-hosted baseline (includes ops + amortized infra): ~$170 per 1M tokens (but with higher engineering/ops risk and slower time-to-recovery).

Key assumptions:
- Token definition: 4 chars/token on average (English).
- Request mix: 60% short prompts (<128 tokens), 40% long (>512 tokens).
- Batching: Redwood runtime benefits from continuous batching and KV cache; we model batch sizes at runtime averages I noted.
- Cache hit: For FintechCo’s use-case we simulated 30/60/90% prefix cache hit curves; the attached workbook shows per-scenario unit savings.
- SLA and support costs: Hyperscale quoted SLA is higher-cost addon in their pricing model; Redwood's Dedicated option (if you need committed throughput) changes the numbers — see workbook for committed curves.

Next tests proposed:
- Concrete run: 1M tokens total, three batch configurations (1/4/16), simulate cache hit at 30/60/90%. Collect p50/p95 latency and per-token cost.
- Redwood will run its side by side from our hosted infra to avoid your infra setup time. We can provide a signed POC terms doc for the two-day test.

Attachments: unit_economics_assumptions.pdf

I’ll wait for you to confirm the test window. If Priya wants the POC terms first, happy to push a short SOW.

Best,
Ben
